# Generator for PNG chunk payload bytes used by lodepng_chunk_create fuzz stub.
# The stub chooses:
#  - length: 0..31
#  - type: four uppercase letters (A-Z)
#  - data: FUZZ_PARAM_STR() -> used as data pointer; if size < length, it is resized with NUL padding
# Our task: return a bytes buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can draw from to produce interesting, yet valid payloads
# for a variety of chunk types. Since the stub allows any 4-letter type and any payload, our buffer should contain
# multiple structured and unstructured snippets to exercise different code paths (e.g., CRC computation on various
# contents, zero/short/exact length handling, ASCII/binary extremes).
#
# Strategy:
#  - Build a small corpus-like buffer by concatenating multiple candidate payload snippets with separators.
#  - Include patterns of sizes from 0 to 31 bytes; ASCII, binary, repetitive, high-entropy (deflate-like) data.
#  - Include plausible PNG chunk payloads for common types (tEXt, iTXt, sRGB, gAMA, pHYs, tIME) but keep each <= 31 bytes.
#  - Provide varying lengths; when the stub requests a certain length, resizing/padding/truncation will yield deterministic
#    slices from this corpus.
#  - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _make_text_chunks() -> list[bytes]:
    # Minimal plausible payloads for some known chunks (without CRC/length/type since lodepng_chunk_create handles those)
    items = []
    # tEXt: key\0text (Latin-1). Keep small.
    items.append(b"k\x00v")  # key="k", text="v"
    items.append(b"Comment\x00Hello")
    # zTXt: key\0compression(0) + compressed text (but any bytes are allowed). Keep tiny placeholder.
    items.append(b"Z\x000\x78\x9c")  # looks like start of zlib, short
    # iTXt: key\0 compflag(0) compmeth(0) lang\0 transkey\0 utf8
    items.append(b"K\x00\x00\x00en\x00tr\x00hi")
    # sRGB: rendering intent (1 byte)
    items.append(b"\x00")
    items.append(b"\x01")
    items.append(b"\x02")
    items.append(b"\x03")
    # gAMA: 4-byte integer gamma*100000 (e.g., 45455 ~ 1/2.2). Use network order.
    items.append(struct.pack(">I", 45455))
    items.append(struct.pack(">I", 100000))
    # pHYs: 9 bytes: X(4) Y(4) unit(1)
    items.append(struct.pack(">IIb", 3780, 3780, 1))
    # tIME: 7 bytes: year(2) month day hour min sec
    items.append(struct.pack(">HBBBBB", 2020, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5))
    # bKGD for truecolor: 6 bytes R,G,B each 2 bytes
    items.append(struct.pack(">HHH", 0xFFFF, 0, 0))
    return items


def _make_binary_patterns(rng: random.Random) -> list[bytes]:
    pats = []
    # Empty and very small
    pats.append(b"")
    pats.append(b"\x00")
    pats.append(b"\xff")
    pats.append(b"\x00\x00\x00\x00")
    pats.append(b"\xff\xff\xff\xff")
    # Repetitive bytes
    pats.append(b"A" * 8)
    pats.append(b"\x00\xff" * 8)
    pats.append(b"\x7f" * 16)
    # Incrementing/decrementing
    pats.append(bytes(range(1, 17)))
    pats.append(bytes(range(255, 255-16, -1)))
    # Random short blobs of various sizes up to 31
    for n in (3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 23, 29, 31):
        pats.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n))
    # Looks like deflate header start + small payload
    pats.append(b"\x78\x01hello")  # no actual deflate integrity, but valid bytes
    pats.append(b"\x78\x9c" + b"X" * 10)
    return pats


def _make_ascii_patterns() -> list[bytes]:
    pats = []
    # Printable ASCII words and edge cases
    pats.append(b"a")
    pats.append(b"A")
    pats.append(b"0")
    pats.append(b" ")
    pats.append(b"\n")
    pats.append(b"Key\x00Value")  # useful for tEXt-like
    pats.append(b"LoremIpsum")
    pats.append(b"PNG")
    pats.append(b"CRCTEST")
    pats.append(b"x" * 31)
    pats.append(b"\x00" + b"txt")
    return pats


def _cap(bufs: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    data = b"|".join(bufs)  # separator unlikely to matter; stub may slice arbitrarily
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        return data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Compose diverse snippets
    parts: list[bytes] = []

    # Include structured chunk-like payloads
    parts.extend(_make_text_chunks())

    # Include ASCII patterns
    parts.extend(_make_ascii_patterns())

    # Include binary patterns (randomized by seed)
    parts.extend(_make_binary_patterns(rng))

    # Add a few short zlib-compressed samples to vary CRC/data distribution, capped length
    # We'll compress small deterministic phrases and truncate to <=31 to remain interesting when length is clamped.
    phrases = [b"hello world", b"aaaaaaaaaaaaaa", b"PNG chunk payload", b"1234567890abcdef"]
    for p in phrases:
        z = zlib.compress(p)
        parts.append(z[:31])

    # Add lengths 0..31 sequences to ensure exact match for any chosen length
    for n in range(0, 32):
        parts.append(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(n))))

    # Slight bias towards NUL-terminated text-like data
    parts.append(b"name\x00value")
    parts.append(b"k\x00")
    parts.append(b"k\x00v\x00")

    # Shuffle groups lightly but deterministically to diversify across seeds
    rng.shuffle(parts)

    return _cap(parts)

# Generator for arbitrary binary data that is still interesting for CRC and (zlib/deflate) compression
# Focus on creating inputs with varied entropy, repeated patterns, small/large ranges, and embedded

MAX_TOTAL = 2048  # keep within fuzzer stub bounds (<= 2048 for save_file; others cap at 1024)

def _rand(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(a, b)

def _weighted_choice(r: random.Random, items: List):
    # items: list of (weight, value)
    total = sum(w for w, _ in items)
    pick = r.uniform(0, total)
    upto = 0.0
    for w, v in items:
        upto += w
        if pick <= upto:
            return v
    return items[-1][1]

def _make_repeated_pattern(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create repeating patterns with varying period
    period = _rand(r, 1, 64)
    token = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(period))
    reps = _rand(r, 1, max(1, MAX_TOTAL // max(1, period)))
    data = (token * reps)[:_rand(r, min(16, len(token)), min(MAX_TOTAL, period * reps))]
    return data

def _make_numeric_sequences(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sequences of incrementing/decrementing numbers in various widths
    width = _weighted_choice(r, [(3,1),(3,2),(2,4)])
    length = _rand(r, 16, MAX_TOTAL // width)
    asc = r.choice([True, False])
    start = _rand(r, 0, (1 << (width*8)) - 1)
    out = bytearray()
    val = start
    for i in range(length):
        if width == 1:
            out.append(val & 0xFF)
        elif width == 2:
            out += struct.pack('>H', val & 0xFFFF)
        else:
            out += struct.pack('>I', val & 0xFFFFFFFF)
        if asc:
            val = (val + 1) & ((1 << (width*8)) - 1)
        else:
            val = (val - 1) & ((1 << (width*8)) - 1)
    return bytes(out)

def _make_low_entropy(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mostly zeros or a single byte value, with occasional spikes
    length = _rand(r, 1, MAX_TOTAL)
    base = r.choice([0x00, 0xFF, r.getrandbits(8)])
    out = bytearray([base]) * length
    for _ in range(_rand(r, 0, length // 64 + 1)):
        pos = _rand(r, 0, length - 1)
        out[pos] = r.getrandbits(8)
    return bytes(out)

def _make_high_entropy(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    length = _rand(r, 1, MAX_TOTAL)
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))

def _make_text_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # ASCII text with newlines and common words
    words = [b"PNG", b"DATA", b"TEST", b"LZ77", b"DEFLATE", b"AAAA", b"BBBB", b"1234567890"]
    lines = _rand(r, 1, 128)
    out = bytearray()
    for _ in range(lines):
        parts = _rand(r, 1, 8)
        for __ in range(parts):
            choice = r.random()
            if choice < 0.5:
                w = r.choice(words)
                out += w
            else:
                # random alphanum run
                run = _rand(r, 1, 40)
                for _k in range(run):
                    chset = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-:."
                    out.append(chset[r.randrange(len(chset))])
            if r.random() < 0.3:
                out.append(ord(' '))
        out += b"\n"
        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

def _make_png_signature_and_chunks(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Not necessarily fully valid PNG, but include correct signature and plausible chunk framing
    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    buf = bytearray(sig)

    def add_chunk(typ: bytes, data: bytes):
        # length + type + data + fake CRC (not necessarily correct; still bytes)
        buf.extend(struct.pack('>I', len(data)))
        buf.extend(typ)
        buf.extend(data)
        # append 4 bytes as placeholder CRC (random)
        buf.extend(struct.pack('>I', r.getrandbits(32)))

    # IHDR 13 bytes
    w = _rand(r, 1, 512)
    h = _rand(r, 1, 512)
    bitdepth = r.choice([1,2,4,8])
    colortype = r.choice([0,2,3,4,6])
    ihdr = struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, bitdepth, colortype, 0, 0, 0)
    add_chunk(b'IHDR', ihdr)

    # optional IDAT-like data (random size)
    idat_sz = _rand(r, 0, 512)
    idat = bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(idat_sz))
    add_chunk(b'IDAT', idat)

    # IEND
    add_chunk(b'IEND', b'')
    return bytes(buf[:MAX_TOTAL])

def _mix_sections(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a composite buffer from several sections to vary compressibility and patterns
    sections = []
    builders = [
        _make_repeated_pattern,
        _make_numeric_sequences,
        _make_low_entropy,
        _make_high_entropy,
        _make_text_like,
        _make_png_signature_and_chunks,
    ]
    # choose 2-5 sections
    for _ in range(_rand(r, 2, 5)):
        b = r.choice(builders)(r)
        sections.append(b)
    data = b"".join(sections)
    # Trim or pad slightly with random bytes to hit a variety of sizes
    target = _rand(r, min(1, len(data)), min(MAX_TOTAL, max(1, len(data))))
    data = data[:target]
    if len(data) == 0:
        data = b"\x00"
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    strategy = _weighted_choice(r, [
        (2, 'repeat'),
        (2, 'numeric'),
        (2, 'low'),
        (2, 'high'),
        (2, 'text'),
        (2, 'pngish'),
        (6, 'mix'),
    ])
    if strategy == 'repeat':
        data = _make_repeated_pattern(r)
    elif strategy == 'numeric':
        data = _make_numeric_sequences(r)
    elif strategy == 'low':
        data = _make_low_entropy(r)
    elif strategy == 'high':
        data = _make_high_entropy(r)
    elif strategy == 'text':
        data = _make_text_like(r)
    elif strategy == 'pngish':
        data = _make_png_signature_and_chunks(r)
    else:
        data = _mix_sections(r)

    # Ensure within global max and non-empty
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"
    return data[:MAX_TOTAL]

import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generates valid raw DEFLATE (RFC1951) streams (no zlib/gzip wrapper)
# Strategy:
# - Compose uncompressed (stored) blocks and/or simple fixed-Huffman blocks
# - For fixed-Huffman, we can safely rely on zlib with -15 window bits to emit raw deflate
# - For stored blocks, build manually with proper headers, length and nlen
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes
# - Vary payload patterns to exercise decompressor paths

MAX_TOTAL_SIZE = 4096

# Helper: create a valid raw DEFLATE stream using zlib with wbits=-15
# level controls compression aggressiveness; data is the uncompressed bytes

def _deflate_fixed(data: bytes, level: int = 1) -> bytes:
    # zlib.compressobj with wbits=-15 emits raw deflate (no zlib wrapper)
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level=level, wbits=-15, strategy=zlib.Z_FIXED)
    out = comp.compress(data) + comp.flush()
    return out

# Helper: build a single stored (uncompressed) block per RFC1951
# BFINAL: 0 or 1, data: bytes (length must fit in <=65535)

def _stored_block(data: bytes, final: bool) -> bytes:
    if len(data) > 65535:
        raise ValueError("stored block data too large")
    bfinal = 1 if final else 0
    btype = 0  # 00 for stored
    header = bytes([(bfinal) | (btype << 1)])
    LEN = len(data)
    NLEN = (~LEN) & 0xFFFF
    # LEN and NLEN are little-endian 16-bit
    len_bytes = struct.pack('<H', LEN)
    nlen_bytes = struct.pack('<H', NLEN)
    return header + len_bytes + nlen_bytes + data

# Helper: split data into multiple stored blocks

def _stored_deflate_stream(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Split into chunks <= 65535
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    i = 0
    total = len(data)
    while i < total:
        take = min(65535, total - i)
        chunk = data[i:i+take]
        i += take
        chunks.append(chunk)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for idx, ch in enumerate(chunks):
        final = (idx == len(chunks) - 1)
        parts.append(_stored_block(ch, final))
    return b''.join(parts)

# Generate various payload patterns to exercise inflater

def _pattern_bytes(kind: int, size: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if size <= 0:
        return b''
    if kind == 0:
        # All zeros
        return bytes([0] * size)
    if kind == 1:
        # All 0xFF
        return bytes([0xFF] * size)
    if kind == 2:
        # Increasing bytes 0..255 wrap
        return bytes([(i & 0xFF) for i in range(size)])
    if kind == 3:
        # Repeated short pattern to allow backreferences
        pat_len = rng.choice([3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 16, 32])
        pat = bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(pat_len))
        return (pat * (size // pat_len + 1))[:size]
    if kind == 4:
        # Random data
        return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(size))
    if kind == 5:
        # Long runs then changes
        out = bytearray()
        val = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        remaining = size
        while remaining > 0:
            run = rng.randint(1, min(512, remaining))
            out.extend([val] * run)
            remaining -= run
            val = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        return bytes(out)
    if kind == 6:
        # Alternating 0x00/0xFF
        return bytes([0x00 if (i & 1) == 0 else 0xFF for i in range(size)])
    # Fallback random
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(size))

# Build a composite deflate stream mixing stored and fixed-huffman blocks

def _composite_deflate(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Decide number of segments
    segments = rng.randint(1, 5)
    total_budget = rng.randint(64, min(2048, MAX_TOTAL_SIZE - 32))
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remaining_budget = total_budget
    for s in range(segments):
        # Choose block type: 0=stored, 1=fixed-huffman
        btype = rng.choice([0, 1, 1])  # slightly bias towards compressed
        seg_size = rng.randint(0, max(0, remaining_budget // (segments - s) if (segments - s) > 0 else remaining_budget))
        seg_size = max(0, min(seg_size, remaining_budget))
        if seg_size == 0 and s < segments - 1:
            continue
        payload_kind = rng.randrange(0, 7)
        payload = _pattern_bytes(payload_kind, seg_size, rng)
        if btype == 0:
            # stored block(s)
            block_bytes = _stored_deflate_stream(payload)
        else:
            # fixed-huffman compressed raw deflate
            level = rng.choice([0, 1, 3, 6])
            block_bytes = _deflate_fixed(payload, level=level)
        parts.append(block_bytes)
        remaining_budget = max(0, remaining_budget - seg_size)
    # Ensure total < MAX_TOTAL_SIZE
    out = b''.join(parts)
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        return out[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
    return out

# Occasionally emit a single carefully constructed stored block to touch adler/length-ignore toggles

def _single_stored_edge(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    size = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 10, 255, 256, 1024, 4095, 8192])
    size = min(size, 2000)  # stay modest
    payload = _pattern_bytes(rng.randrange(0, 7), size, rng)
    return _stored_deflate_stream(payload)

# Occasionally emit a fixed-huffman stream with very compressible data

def _fixed_huffman_run(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    size = rng.randint(32, 2048)
    payload = _pattern_bytes(3, size, rng)  # repeated pattern
    return _deflate_fixed(payload, level=rng.choice([0, 1, 6]))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        stream = _single_stored_edge(rng)
    elif choice < 0.6:
        stream = _fixed_huffman_run(rng)
    else:
        stream = _composite_deflate(rng)
    # Ensure size bound
    if len(stream) > MAX_TOTAL_SIZE:
        stream = stream[:MAX_TOTAL_SIZE]
    # Also ensure the fuzzer stub caps at 1024, so bias toward <=1024 length
    if len(stream) > 1024 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        stream = stream[:1024]
    return bytes(stream)

# This generator produces valid RFC1950 zlib streams (2-byte header + DEFLATE data + Adler32)
# suitable for APIs expecting zlib-formatted input. It crafts a variety of valid compressed
# payloads and compression strategies to exercise different decompression paths.

# Limit final buffer to <= 4096 bytes as required.
MAX_OUT = 4096

# Some interesting raw payload patterns to compress
PAYLOAD_PATTERNS: List[Tuple[str, bytes]] = [
    ("empty", b""),
    ("zeros_short", b"\x00" * 16),
    ("zeros_long", b"\x00" * 512),
    ("ascii_text", b"Hello, LodePNG! " * 16),
    ("high_entropy", bytes(range(256)) * 2),
    ("repeating_blocks", (b"ABCD" * 64) + (b"EFGH" * 64)),
    ("increasing_bytes", bytes([i % 256 for i in range(1024)])),
    ("pal_like", bytes([i // 4 for i in range(1024)])),
    ("png_signature_only", b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"),
    ("small_json", b"{\"k\":1,\"arr\":[0,1,2,3]}" * 8),
    ("utf8_text", ("\u2603 snowman ".encode("utf-8") * 32)),
]

# Different zlib wrapper strategies (wbits=+15 for zlib, levels/strategies vary)
ZLIB_LEVELS = [0, 1, 3, 6, 9]
ZLIB_STRATEGIES = [zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, zlib.Z_FILTERED, zlib.Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY, zlib.Z_RLE, zlib.Z_FIXED]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _random_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a pattern and optionally vary size
    name, base = rng.choice(PAYLOAD_PATTERNS)
    # Occasionally generate a random binary payload of varied size
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        size = rng.randint(0, 2048)
        return _rand_bytes(rng, size)
    # Occasionally slice or extend the base
    if len(base) > 0 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        # slice
        start = 0
        end = rng.randint(0, len(base))
        return base[start:end]
    # or repeat some times
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        reps = rng.randint(1, 8)
        return (base * reps)[:2048]
    return base


def _make_zlib(data: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Use zlib.compressobj to control params; ensure RFC1950 wrapper (wbits=+15)
    level = rng.choice(ZLIB_LEVELS)
    strategy = rng.choice(ZLIB_STRATEGIES)

    # Sometimes tweak memLevel and wbits for variety
    memLevel = rng.randint(1, 9)
    wbits = 15  # zlib wrapper

    # Create compressor
    comp = zlib.compressobj(level=level, method=zlib.DEFLATED, wbits=wbits, memLevel=memLevel, strategy=strategy)
    comped = comp.compress(data) + comp.flush()

    # The zlib module already produces a valid RFC1950 stream (CMF/FLG + DEFLATE + Adler32)
    return comped


def _ensure_size(buf: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Keep within MAX_OUT; if larger, try with higher compression or different payload
    if len(buf) <= MAX_OUT:
        return buf
    # Recompress with max compression and different strategy
    try:
        comp = zlib.compressobj(level=9, method=zlib.DEFLATED, wbits=15, memLevel=9, strategy=zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY)
        smaller = comp.compress(zlib.decompress(buf)) + comp.flush()
        if len(smaller) <= MAX_OUT:
            return smaller
    except Exception:
        pass
    # As a fallback, truncate the raw payload and recompress
    try:
        raw = zlib.decompress(buf)
        raw = raw[:max(0, int(len(raw) * 0.5))]
        buf2 = _make_zlib(raw, rng)
        if len(buf2) <= MAX_OUT:
            return buf2
    except Exception:
        pass
    # Final fallback: compress empty
    return _make_zlib(b"", rng)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose or synthesize a payload
    payload = _random_payload(rng)

    # Optionally concatenate segments to form multi-block deflate streams
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        segments = [payload]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            segments.append(_random_payload(rng))
        payload = b"".join(segments)
        # Keep raw payload size modest
        if len(payload) > 4096:
            payload = payload[:4096]

    # Create a valid zlib stream
    z = _make_zlib(payload, rng)

    # Sometimes wrap multiple independent zlib members concatenated (valid for some inflaters)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        extra_payload = _random_payload(rng)
        z2 = _make_zlib(extra_payload, rng)
        z = z + z2

    # Enforce maximum output size
    z = _ensure_size(z, rng)

    # Ensure non-empty to exercise code paths expecting some input
    if not z:
        z = _make_zlib(b"A", rng)
        z = _ensure_size(z, rng)

    # As a final safeguard, cap to MAX_OUT bytes (zlib streams remain valid when members are whole).
    # We avoid truncating inside a member; only truncate if multiple members and boundary known.
    if len(z) > MAX_OUT:
        # Try to split by detecting start of second member: decompress first, then recompress first only
        try:
            # Attempt to decompress the first member only by incremental decompressor
            decomp = zlib.decompressobj(wbits=15)
            decomp.decompress(z)
            tail = decomp.unused_data
            first_len = len(z) - len(tail)
            if first_len > 0:
                z = z[:first_len]
        except Exception:
            # If detection fails, regenerate a smaller single-member stream
            z = _ensure_size(_make_zlib(payload[:512], rng), rng)
    return z

import os
import random
import struct
import time

# Generator for a narrow (char*) filesystem path used by lodepng load/save wrappers.
# The fuzzer harness uses two sources:
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): expects a filename to read from or write to.
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): arbitrary byte buffer (limited by harness to <=2048 bytes).
# Our single bytes output must carry initial interesting data usable for both.
# Strategy:
#  - Create a small, valid PNG file in a temporary-like relative path to exercise load paths.
#  - Also embed an arbitrary small PNG along with some non-PNG data to exercise save paths.
#  - Since we cannot perform I/O here, we only provide bytes; the fuzzer infra will map this
#    buffer both to filenames and to data. Therefore, we structure the buffer as:
#    [Sectioned blob]
#    - A NUL-terminated relative filename (ASCII), followed by another NUL-terminated alt name.
#    - Then one or more file images (PNG bytes) that the harness may use for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Filenames are relative, simple, and ASCII-only to satisfy narrow-path expectation.

PNG_SIG = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"


def _crc32(data: bytes) -> int:
    # PNG CRC is standard CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, polynomial 0xEDB88320), same as zlib/crc32.
    # Use binascii.crc32 which matches.
    import binascii
    return binascii.crc32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _png_chunk(typ: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    length = struct.pack(">I", len(data))
    crc = struct.pack(">I", _crc32(typ + data))
    return length + typ + data + crc


def _pack_ihdr(width: int, height: int, bitdepth: int, colortype: int, interlace: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # compression=0, filter=0 per PNG spec
    return struct.pack(
        ">IIBBBBB",
        width,
        height,
        bitdepth,
        colortype,
        0,  # compression
        0,  # filter
        interlace,
    )


def _adler32(data: bytes) -> int:
    import zlib
    return zlib.adler32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF


def _zlib_uncompressed_block(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Build a zlib stream (CMF/FLG + single uncompressed DEFLATE block + Adler32)
    # Use window size 32K and no compression: CMF=0x78, FLG=0x01 (FCHECK adjusted for CMF)
    # 0x78 0x01 is a common zlib header for no-compression/fastest.
    cmf = 0x78
    flg = 0x01
    # Build one uncompressed block (BFINAL=1, BTYPE=00)
    bfinal_btype = b"\x01"
    # LEN and NLEN 16-bit little endian
    ln = len(payload)
    len_le = struct.pack("<H", ln)
    nlen_le = struct.pack("<H", (~ln) & 0xFFFF)
    block = bfinal_btype + len_le + nlen_le + payload
    ad = struct.pack(">I", _adler32(payload))
    return bytes([cmf, flg]) + block + ad


def _make_png_rgba_solid(w: int, h: int, rgba: tuple[int, int, int, int]) -> bytes:
    # Create a minimal, valid PNG with uncompressed IDAT data for a solid-color image.
    # Color type 6 (RGBA), bit depth 8.
    # Each scanline: filter byte (0) + w*4 bytes
    r, g, b, a = rgba
    row = bytes([0]) + bytes([r, g, b, a]) * w
    raw = row * h
    z = _zlib_uncompressed_block(raw)
    ihdr = _png_chunk(b"IHDR", _pack_ihdr(w, h, 8, 6, 0))
    idat = _png_chunk(b"IDAT", z)
    iend = _png_chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    return PNG_SIG + ihdr + idat + iend


def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random, prefix: str, ext: str) -> bytes:
    # Generate simple ASCII filename: prefix + random hex + ext
    salt = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 8)))
    name = f"{prefix}_{salt}.{ext}"
    return name.encode('ascii') + b"\x00"


def _palette_png_small() -> bytes:
    # Create a tiny 2x2 paletted PNG with tRNS demonstrating palette+alpha path.
    # PLTE with 2 colors, tRNS to make first entry transparent.
    w, h = 2, 2
    ihdr = _png_chunk(b"IHDR", _pack_ihdr(w, h, 8, 3, 0))  # indexed color, 8-bit indices for simplicity
    # Palette: two colors
    plte = _png_chunk(b"PLTE", bytes([255, 0, 0, 0, 255, 0]))  # Red, Green
    trns = _png_chunk(b"tRNS", bytes([0, 255]))  # alpha for entries: transparent, opaque
    # Indices: 0,1 rows
    row0 = bytes([0, 0, 1])  # filter 0 + two pixels
    row1 = bytes([0, 1, 0])
    raw = row0 + row1
    z = _zlib_uncompressed_block(raw)
    idat = _png_chunk(b"IDAT", z)
    iend = _png_chunk(b"IEND", b"")
    return PNG_SIG + ihdr + plte + trns + idat + iend


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build two filenames: one for reading (points to likely-existing content created by fuzzer infra),
    # and one for writing. Using relative names to avoid path parsing edge cases.
    fname_read = _rand_filename(rng, "in", "png")
    fname_write = _rand_filename(rng, "out", "png")

    # Create a few small valid PNG images covering different color types to feed into FUZZ_PARAM_STR usages.
    # Sizes capped to keep total under 4096 bytes.
    imgs: list[bytes] = []
    # Solid RGBA 1x1 and 4x4 with different alphas
    imgs.append(_make_png_rgba_solid(1, 1, (0, 0, 0, 0)))
    imgs.append(_make_png_rgba_solid(4, 4, (rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), rng.randrange(256), 255)))
    # Small paletted image with tRNS
    imgs.append(_palette_png_small())

    # Also append some arbitrary raw data which save_file paths will write as-is.
    # Keep it small; include PNG signature prefix to appear file-like, followed by random bytes.
    raw_prefix = PNG_SIG[:4] + os.urandom(8)
    raw_tail = rng.randbytes(32) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes([rng.randrange(256) for _ in range(32)])
    raw_blob = raw_prefix + raw_tail

    # Assemble the final buffer:
    # [fname_read NUL][fname_write NUL][u32 count][for each: u32 len + data][u32 raw_len + raw_blob]
    out = bytearray()
    out += fname_read
    out += fname_write

    # Pack images
    out += struct.pack(">I", len(imgs) + 1)  # include raw blob as last entry
    for img in imgs:
        out += struct.pack(">I", len(img))
        out += img
    out += struct.pack(">I", len(raw_blob))
    out += raw_blob

    # Ensure size cap
    return bytes(out[:4096])
